title: Decoding Plasticity Regulators and Transition Trajectories in Glioblastoma with Single-cell Multiomics
authors: Saraswat M; Rueda-Gensini L; Heinzelmann E; Gracia T; Memi F; de Jong G; Straub J; Schloo C; Hoffmann DC; Jung E; Kindinger T; Weigel B; Lim B; Weil S; Gould O; Mair R; Mikulik K; Rohbeck M; Wick W; Winkler F; Bayraktar OA; Stegle O; Mall M
one_liner_zh: 该文用单细胞多组学和深度学习推断增强子驱动的基因调控网络，研究胶质母细胞瘤细胞状态可塑性及转录因子MYT1L的调控作用，虽涉及TF-DNA调控网络但非直接结合建模，方法可迁移至TF-DNA互作研究。
abstract: Glioblastoma (GB) is one of the most lethal human cancers, marked by profound intratumoral heterogeneity and near-universal treatment resistance. Cellular plasticity, the capacity of cancer cells to transition between phenotypic states, drives GB progression and resistance. However, the regulatory logic that permits or restricts specific state transitions remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated single-nucleus RNA and chromatin accessibility multi-ome profiles from over one million cells across primary IDH-wildtype GBs and developed scDORI, a scalable deep-learning framework to infer enhancer-driven gene regulatory networks (eGRNs) at single-cell resolution. Our analysis revealed a structured hierarchy of GB cell states governed by distinct regulatory programs, with marked variability in epigenetic plasticity that enables or constrains transitions. Neuronal-like tumor cells emerge as a low plasticity state that deploys active repression, in contrast to more permissive progenitor-like and astrocytic states. We identified the neuronal-like state-specific repressor MYT1L as a key regulator that silences master transcription factors of alternative states. MYT1L gain-of-function in patient-derived GB cells reduced chromatin accessibility, induced neuronal-like identity, and restricted proliferation and invasion in vivo, whereas loss-of-function reactivated plasticity and accelerated malignant features. Our findings delineate the epigenetic architecture and associated transcriptional master regulators that shape GB state trajectories, and establish safeguard repressors such as MYT1L as potential therapeutic targets to constrain malignant plasticity.
abstract_zh: 胶质母细胞瘤 (Glioblastoma, GB) 是最致命的人类癌症之一，其特征是显著的瘤内异质性和近乎普遍的耐药性。细胞可塑性，即癌细胞在不同表型状态之间转换的能力，驱动着GB的进展和耐药性。然而，允许或限制特定状态转换的调控逻辑仍知之甚少。在此，我们整合了来自原发IDH野生型GB的超过一百万个细胞的单核RNA和染色质可及性多组学图谱，并开发了scDORI，一种可扩展的深度学习框架，用于在单细胞分辨率下推断增强子驱动的基因调控网络 (enhancer-driven gene regulatory networks, eGRNs)。我们的分析揭示了由不同调控程序支配的GB细胞状态的结构化层级，其表观遗传可塑性存在显著差异，从而促进或限制状态转换。神经元样肿瘤细胞表现为一种低可塑性状态，部署主动抑制，而更宽松的祖细胞样和星形胶质细胞样状态则相反。我们鉴定了神经元样状态特异性抑制因子MYT1L，作为沉默替代状态主转录因子的关键调控因子。在患者来源的GB细胞中，MYT1L功能获得降低了染色质可及性，诱导神经元样身份，并在体内限制增殖和侵袭，而功能丧失则重新激活可塑性并加速恶性特征。我们的发现描绘了塑造GB状态轨迹的表观遗传架构及相关转录主调控因子，并确立了如MYT1L等保护性抑制因子作为限制恶性可塑性的潜在治疗靶点。
